subject: Anesthesia
title: Malignant Hyperthermia: Recognize the Anesthetic Emergency
preview: Malignant hyperthermia is a hypermetabolic anesthetic crisis; rapid recognition and removal of triggering agents are vital.

sections.title: Mechanism and recognition
points: Dysregulated skeletal-muscle calcium release drives hypermetabolism, heat production and muscle breakdown.
Hyperthermia may develop after earlier physiologic abnormalities; waiting for a high temperature may delay recognition.

sections.title: Emergency management
points: Stop triggering agents, ventilate with oxygen, administer dantrolene according to the current crisis protocol and correct complications.
Monitor electrolytes, rhythm, kidney function, temperature and recurrence risk.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Dantrolene is a specific therapy; naloxone is not the reversal agent for malignant hyperthermia.
Early ETCO2 rise may be more informative than a late fever spike.

quickRevision: Triggering volatile anesthetics and succinylcholine can provoke malignant hyperthermia in susceptible patients.
Early clues include rising end-tidal carbon dioxide, tachycardia, rigidity and metabolic or respiratory acidosis.
Stop triggers, call for help, give dantrolene and provide intensive physiological support using a rehearsed protocol.

quiz.question: Which drug is specifically used to treat malignant hyperthermia?
quiz.explanation: Dantrolene is a specific therapy; naloxone is not the reversal agent for malignant hyperthermia.
